amendments.because: Listing every test in the new fix's Done-when duplicates next's lines and grows without limit; the fix names the failed run instead
amendments.done_when: When the latest nightly full run failed, forge next names the platforms and failing tests and gives the forge fix start command for them

done_when: When the latest scheduled run of a workflow failed, forge next names its failed jobs and every failing test, and gives one forge fix start command for that failed run (or the started fix's next step)

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. The test parser accepts only `FAILED` summary lines. Pytest also reports a test whose fixture fails during setup or teardown as `ERROR tests/...::test_name`; that test is omitted from `forge next` even though its scheduled job failed. The named command-level proof supplies only `FAILED` lines, so it passes in this case. [Pytest's output documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/example/simple.html) shows this summary format.
findings.title: Not done: When the latest scheduled run of a workflow failed, forge next names its failed jobs and every failing test, and gives one forge f

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 3, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. This fetch caps the combined list at 100 runs before selecting each workflow's latest run. If another workflow runs every five minutes, its 100 runs displace a failed daily run after about eight hours; `forge next` then stops reporting that daily workflow even though its latest run failed. The proof uses only three runs. [GitHub permits five-minute schedules](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax).
findings.title: Not done: a frequent scheduled workflow hides a failed daily run

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. This selects a command from the fix's stored status. After `forge close`, the stored status can be `waiting for checks`, while `_item_readiness` in `src/forge/nextstep.py:669-680` derives `ready` when checks pass or `checks failed` when they fail. The scheduled-run alert says `forge close` in both cases instead of the merge or repair step that the existing fix report gives. Because the alert precedes that report, `forge next --json` also selects its wrong command. The proof checks only a fix still in `started` status.
findings.title: A started fix can be given the wrong next command

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 3, Harm 2
The parser requires a pytest-style `FAILED path::test` line. A client repo using the shipped JavaScript stack can have a scheduled Jest or Vitest job with named failing tests but no such line, so `forge next` lists the job without its tests. The shipped guidance names Jest and Vitest in `src/forge/templates/skill.md:722`, and [Vitest documents a different test reporter format](https://main.vitest.dev/guide/reporters.html). This is an additional language case.
findings.title: Follow-up: name Jest and Vitest failures in scheduled runs

stop.reason: Coordinator (Harm 2, reversible): the generated fix names the failed jobs and the run, not every test (forge next's lines already name every test); a fix started on another machine gets the plain line that it runs on that machine, like other remote items.

why: A failing nightly full run on macOS or Windows is easy to miss, and Windows stayed red for days unseen
